page: Amazon Web Services g7e.24xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The platform features 96 dedicated vCPUs derived from 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8559C processor clocked at 2.4 GHz, supported by 320 MB of L3 cache alongside AMX and AVX-512 vector extensions. System memory provides 1024.0 GB of DDR5 operating at 6 GHz, supplying 10.67 GB of RAM per physical core. Accelerator hardware consists of four NVIDIA Blackwell RTX PRO 6000 GPUs providing an aggregate 384 GB of VRAM. Complementing the compute core is 7600 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and an 800 Gbps baseline network bandwidth interface.

Benchmark evaluations position this instance in the top tier for compute, memory, and accelerator workloads. The system attained a Geekbench multi-core score of 21470 and a PassMark CPU score of 91429.15, backed by multi-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput of 564.58 GB/sec. The quad-GPU configuration delivers 95118 in ray tracing tests. In large language model inference tests, the system produced 1278.65 prompt tokens per second and 28.21 generation tokens per second on 70B parameter models, expanding to 7144.93 prompt tokens per second on 7B models. Memory subsystem bandwidth reaches 224.52 GB/sec on large block reads, contributing to Redis performance exceeding 102 million SET operations per second.

The dense co-location of 384 GB GPU memory, 1 TB DDR5 system memory, and 7.6 TB NVMe storage reduces inter-node data transfer bottlenecks, enhancing operational efficiency for large computational pipelines. Maximizing this resource efficiency requires fully utilizing all four accelerators and the high-bandwidth networking stack, as idle capacity carries substantial overhead. The g7e.24xlarge is structured for large-scale AI inference, model fine-tuning, complex 3D graphics rendering, video processing, and data-intensive applications demanding integrated GPU acceleration and high I/O throughput.

The system incorporates 7600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and an 800 Gbps baseline network interface.
